react_native_issues.issue: On Expo Web preview, the iris translateX animation does not propagate to the DOM: getComputedStyle(iris ).transform stays 'none' across ~2.5s. Only the outer Animated.View scaleY blink is visible (matrix scaleY seen dipping to 0.7996). Likely cause: useNativeDriver:true on web falls back to JS driver and the Animated.Image's interpolated translateX is not written to style on web. Recommended fix: wrap the animated iris in an Animated.View (not Animated.Image) OR set useNativeDriver:false on web via Platform.select, so the JS driver writes the transform to style. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/EyeLoader.tsx:78-91. Native (iOS/Android) is expected to still work — no red screen, no console error.

action_items: OPTIONAL/COSMETIC (web only): In /app/frontend/src/components/EyeLoader.tsx, either (a) wrap the <Animated.Image IRIS> inside an <Animated.View> that owns the translateX transform, or (b) use useNativeDriver: Platform.OS !== 'web' so the JS-driver path on web actually writes the interpolated translateX to the DOM. Currently on Expo Web the iris is stationary (only the container blink renders). Native platforms unaffected.

rca_of_issue: Iris translateX not visible on Expo Web preview: react-native-web renders Animated.Image style updates, but with useNativeDriver:true the driver is bypassed on web and the JS fallback occasionally does not push interpolated transforms into the DOM style attribute for <Animated.Image> as reliably as for <Animated.View>. Verified by getComputedStyle(iris).transform staying 'none' while the sibling Animated.View (loader root) DID show a live matrix update on scaleY. Suggested mitigation is above.
